problem: Traditional VLN trains on large labeled datasets, and existing LLM-as-planner embodied agents make a single global plan, so one failed subtask (obstacle, changed target state) makes the following subtasks fail.
motivation: LLMs hold commonsense knowledge that could cut labeling cost, but execution-time errors need feedback and dynamic re-planning. The paper argues an LLM-centric planner needs auxiliary correction and memory/experience mechanisms to complete instructions reliably in few-shot settings.
key_idea: CPMI centers an LLM planner and adds auxiliary modules for correction, memory and generalized experience so the LLM can dynamically re-plan during execution.
insight: Only the abstract is available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract claims that feeding execution feedback and memory/experience back to the LLM planner improves success rate and efficiency in the few-shot setting.
method: LLM-centric planner: decomposes the instruction into a sequence of subtasks and re-plans dynamically.
Correction module: gives feedback on failed subtasks (e.g. obstacles, target state changes) so the plan can be adjusted.
Memory module: stores execution history and gives it to the planner as context.
Generalized experience mechanism: reuses past experience to improve performance during execution.

setting.backbone: LLM (specific model not stated in abstract)
setting.training_data: few-shot; no large labeled training (details not in abstract)

results: The abstract claims the best performance in the few-shot scenario on public datasets, with a higher success rate and better efficiency on successive tasks. No numbers or named baselines are given.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so specifics are unverified.
